To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

affinity labelling of the 70 S initiation complexes of Escherichiacoli ribosomes with 14C-labelled AUGU3[CH2Cl] derivative in the presence of the initiation factors resulted in cross-linking of protein S5, S6, S7, L1, and L16 with the initiator tRNA.
the affinity labelling with 2', 3'-O-[14C]CHRCL AUGU3 derivative of AUGU sequence in the 70 S initiation complexes resulted in the labelling of proteins S5, S9, S16, L1, and IF-2.

the 2'-3'-O-[14C]-labelled AUGU3 derivative is able to bind to the ribosomal 30S subunit in the absence of initiation factors and to form a stable complex with the 70S ribosome in the presence of IF-2.

the affinity labelling of the ribosome with the AUGU3[2',3'-14C]CHRCL analogue in the 70 S initiation complexes obtained with use of initiation factor(s).

the affinity labelling of the 30S subunit of Escherichiacoli ribosome in the initiation complexes with the 2'3'-O-[N-(2-chloretely)-N-methylaminobenzylidene] derivative of AUGU 3 (AUGU 3[14C ]CHRCl) in the presence of fMet-tRNA (Metf).

The main takeaway from our work is that
ribosomes can form initiation complexes in different ways and that the way of the initiation complex formation determines the affinity labelling of the ribosomal components.
the initiation factors are not only involved in the formation of the initiation complex but they also influence the structure of the complex and its affinity to the affinity label.
the affinity modification of ribosomal complexes is a useful tool for the identification of proteins involved in the formation of the ribosomal initiation complex.
